A Practical Synthesis of Chiral Oxazolines through a Highly
Diastereoselective Coupling–Cyclization Reaction of N-(Buta-2,3-
dienyl)amides and Aryl Iodides
Nan Wang,[a] Bo Chen, [b] and Shengming Ma* [a, b]
Introduction
Among organic chemists, the synthesis of optically active
oxazoline derivatives is of great interest because of their
extensive use as chiral auxiliaries and ligands for asymmet-
ric synthesis.
[1] Moreover, numerous oxazoline-containing
compounds, which include natural products and synthetic
drugs, exhibit valuable pharmaceutical properties and have
been widely studied in medicinal chemistry.
[2] General syn-
thetic routes to chiral oxazolines have relied on chiral
amino alcohols as sources
[3] and are, therefore, limited by
the diversity of substituents available and the absolute con-
figurations of the commercially available natural amino
acids. Therefore, the development of efficient strategies for
the preparation of multisubstituted chiral oxazolines is
highly desirable. Recently, our group reported an efficient
preparation of N-(buta-2,3-dienyl)amides from terminal N-
propargyl amides.
[4] The obtained N-allenyl amides were
successfully converted into a variety of oxazoline deriva-
tives via a palladium-catalyzed coupling–cyclization reac-
tion with organic iodides.
[5] As we know, a substituent a to
the allene moiety always has a significant impact on the ste-
reoselectivity of reactions that furnish five-membered cyclic
compounds.
[6] Consequently, we envisioned that the palladi-
um-catalyzed coupling–cyclization reaction of a-substituted
N-(buta-2,3-dienyl)amides may afford trisubstituted oxazo-
line derivatives with high diastereoselectivity through 1,2-
induction. Moreover, optically active oxazolines may be
easily prepared through this strategy by involving optically
active N-(buta-2,3-dienyl)amides.
Results and Discussion
To investigate the diastereoselectivity of the coupling–cycli-
zation reaction, N-(buta-2,3-dienyl)amides 4a –4f were pre-
pared by a Mitsunobu reaction [7] of the corresponding prop-
argyl alcohol 1 followed by a condensation reaction with
benzoyl chloride [8] and then an allenylation step with CuI/
Cy2NH[4] (Scheme 1). It is noteworthy that a Ritter reac-
tion[9] can be used in the synthesis of (1-phenylprop-2-ynyl)-
amine when R is a phenyl group.
With the N-allenyl amides in hand, we carried out the re-
action of 4 with aromatic iodides 5 under the standard con-
ditions that included Pd ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(PPh3)4 (1 mol %), K2CO3 (2 equiv),
and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) at 80 8C.[4] Diverse a-
substituted N-(buta-2,3-dienyl)amides 4 and different aro-
matic iodides 5 were submitted to the reaction conditions
(Table 1). Moderate to good yields and high diastereoselec-
tivities were obtained in most cases. Only the reaction with
4c afforded the corresponding oxazoline derivative 6c a in
a lower isolated yield of 67 % with 20 % of remaining start-
ing material. In the instance of 4d , the corresponding oxa-
zoline derivative 6d a was formed with a relatively low dia-
stereoselectivity (94:6). When R

methyl (i.e., 5c ), or bromo (i.e., 5d ) group did not alter the

Abstract: A highly trans diastereoselective synthesis of 2,4,5-trisubstituted oxa-
zoline derivatives is described that proceeds through a palladium-catalyzed cou-

enantioenriched oxazoline derivatives with excellent 1,2-induction.

diastereoselectivity in the cyclization step is thermodynami-
cally controlled, in which the oxygen anion attacks from
the side to ensure the trans orientation of the R group and
vinylic unit (Scheme 3).
Conclusions
To summarize, we have de-
veloped a procedure for the
highly trans diastereoselec-
tive synthesis of trisubstitut-
ed oxazoline derivatives
through the palladium-cata-
lyzed coupling–cyclization
reaction of a-substituted N-
(buta-2,3-dienyl)amides with aromatic iodides. This method
is particularly advantageous for the efficient introduction of
different substituents along with excellent substrate control

Experimental Section
General Information
All reactions were carried out in oven-dried Schlenk tubes. DMF,
CH3CN, CH2Cl2 were dried over calcium hydride before distillation. 1,4-
Dioxane and THF were dried over Na wire before distillation. All the
temperatures refer to the bath temperature. The
1H NMR chemical
shifts were reported in ppm relative to TMS ( d = 0.00 ppm). The
13C NMR chemical shifts were reported in ppm relative to CDCl 3 (d =
77.0 ppm). IR spectra were recorded on an infrared spectrometer. Melt-
ing points were measured without correction. Common reagents were
purchased from commercial sources and were used without further pu-
rification. Column chromatography was performed using silica gel (300–
400 mesh) and eluting with ethyl acetate and petroleum ether. TLC was
performed with glass-backed silica plates. The chiral propargyl alcohols
(S)-4f ,( S)-4b, and ( S)-4e were synthesized as reported in the litera-
ture.
